models_evaluated: CSA-GPT (instruction-configured Custom GPT built on GPT-5.2)

links.outcome: Reading grade level (FKGL) of patient-facing LLM responses with vs without instruction configuration
links.effect: Mean FKGL 6.07 ± 1.28 for CSA-GPT vs 9.12 ± 1.71 for ChatGPT5.2 (p < 0.001); in-target (6–8) 37.5% vs 25.0%.
links.quote: Mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was 6.07 ± 1.28 (95% CI: 5.79–6.36) for CSA-GPT and 9.12 ± 1.71 (95% CI: 8.74–9.50) for ChatGPT5.2 ( p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Plain-language readability, practicality and structure of AI patient education responses with instruction configuration
links.effect: CSA-GPT had lower FKGL (6.07 vs 9.12), higher practicality (4.92 vs 4.45) and structural clarity (4.50 vs 3.19), all p < 0.001.
links.quote: Mean structural clarity scores were 4.50 ± 0.69 (95% CI: 4.35–4.65) for CSA-GPT and 3.19 ± 0.81 (95% CI: 3.01–3.37) for ChatGPT5.2 (all p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Empathetic tone and linguistic appropriateness of generative AI patient communications rated by specialists
links.effect: Empathy scores 4.45 ± 0.69 for CSA-GPT vs 3.39 ± 0.77 for ChatGPT5.2 (p < 0.001).
links.quote: Mean empathetic tone scores were 4.45 ± 0.69 (95% CI: 4.30–4.60) and 3.39 ± 0.77 (95% CI: 3.22–3.56), respectively.

links.outcome: Inclusion of mandatory professional-consultation disclaimer in AI responses
links.effect: Disclaimer present in 100% (80/80) of CSA-GPT responses vs 0% of ChatGPT5.2 responses.
links.quote: Safety boundary-setting showed complete separation: all 80 CSA-GPT responses included the required professional disclaimer, compared with none of the baseline responses ( Table 3 , Figure 2 ).

links.outcome: Critical omissions of contraindications or major factual errors in LLM dental responses (safety audit)
links.effect: 3/80 ChatGPT5.2 (3.75%) had critical omissions; 1/80 CSA-GPT (1.25%) flagged; no dangerous misinformation; difference not significant (p = 0.25).
links.quote: Three of 80 ChatGPT5.2 responses (3.75%) were flagged for critical omissions, such as failing to explicitly contraindicate whitening in cases of unrestored caries.
